nodes.title: Creative Exploration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify a variety of ways people make art and choose materials to explore an idea.

nodes.title: Basic Art Skills
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name basic art tools (pencil, brush, crayon) and the mark or effect each one makes.

nodes.title: Creative Techniques
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can match a common art technique (blending, layering, stippling) to the effect it produces.

nodes.title: Artistic Expression
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how an artist's choices of color, subject, and mark convey a mood or idea.

nodes.title: Creative Collaboration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe roles and give constructive feedback within a group art project.

nodes.title: Production & Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can order the stages of a design/production workflow from brief to finished piece.

nodes.title: Creative Iteration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how critique feedback is used to revise a work across multiple drafts.

nodes.title: Specialization
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the focus and required skills of a chosen art specialization.

nodes.title: Creative Mastery
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can articulate a personal artistic voice and the body of work that demonstrates it.

nodes.title: Visual Arts
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish major visual-art forms (drawing, painting, sculpture, print) by their media.

nodes.title: Digital Art & Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify which tasks suit raster vs. vector tools in a digital art workflow.

nodes.title: Advanced Creative Projects
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can outline the plan, milestones, and deliverables of a self-directed capstone project.

nodes.title: Music & Rhythm Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify steady beat and simple rhythm patterns by ear.

nodes.title: Theater & Acting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify basic stage roles and the elements of a scene (character, setting, conflict).

nodes.title: Film & Media Production
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify common shot types and the stages of a film production pipeline.

nodes.title: Creative Writing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify narrative structure elements (arc, character, conflict) in a short story.

nodes.title: Line
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify line types (straight, curved, zigzag, implied) and the quality each conveys.

nodes.title: Shape
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish geometric from organic shapes and identify positive vs. negative shape.

nodes.title: Form
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify a 3D form (cube, sphere, cylinder, cone) as the volumetric version of a 2D shape.

nodes.title: Space
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how overlap, size, and placement create the illusion of near and far (depth).

nodes.title: Texture
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish actual (tactile) texture from implied (visual) texture in an artwork.

nodes.title: Value & Perspective
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can order values on a light-to-dark scale and identify how value creates form and contrast.

nodes.title: Color Theory
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify primary, secondary, and tertiary colors and their positions on the color wheel.

nodes.title: Color Harmonies
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify complementary, analogous, and triadic color schemes on the color wheel.

nodes.title: Color Temperature & Properties
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can classify colors as warm or cool and identify a hue's value and saturation.

nodes.title: Color Mixing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can predict the result of mixing two given pigments, including tints and shades.

nodes.title: Visual Design Principles
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can name the principles of design (balance, contrast, emphasis, movement, pattern, proportion, unity).

nodes.title: Balance
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can classify a composition's balance as symmetrical, asymmetrical, or radial.

nodes.title: Contrast
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify where value, color, or size contrast is used to create visual interest.

nodes.title: Emphasis
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the focal point of a composition and the means used to emphasize it.

nodes.title: Movement & Rhythm
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how line, repetition, and placement lead the eye through a composition.

nodes.title: Pattern
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify repeating motifs and distinguish regular from random pattern.

nodes.title: Proportion
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can compare relative sizes of parts to a whole and identify correct vs. distorted proportion.

nodes.title: Unity & Variety
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how repetition creates unity while contrast adds variety in a composition.

nodes.title: Composition
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how the elements and principles are arranged to organize a picture plane.

nodes.title: Rule of Thirds & Focal Point
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can apply the rule of thirds to locate a strong focal-point placement in a composition.

nodes.title: Foundational Drawing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify basic drawing marks and the correct grip and stroke for controlled lines.

nodes.title: Linear Perspective
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify one-, two-, and three-point perspective by their vanishing points.

nodes.title: Gesture Drawing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the line of action that captures a pose's motion and weight.

nodes.title: Anatomy
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify major body landmarks and proportions used to construct the human figure.

nodes.title: Figure Drawing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify standard head-count proportions of the human figure.

nodes.title: Storytelling
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how sequence, framing, and composition convey a narrative in visual art.

nodes.title: Basic Painting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify basic brush techniques (wash, dry brush, blending) and their effects.

nodes.title: Pastels
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify blending and layering techniques specific to soft and oil pastels.

nodes.title: Oil Techniques
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify oil-paint techniques such as glazing, impasto, and fat-over-lean layering.

nodes.title: Watercolor
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify watercolor techniques (wet-on-wet, wet-on-dry, lifting) by their result.

nodes.title: Acrylic
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify properties of acrylic paint (fast drying, layerable) and matching techniques.

nodes.title: Charcoal
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify charcoal techniques (hatching, smudging, lifting with eraser) and their values.

nodes.title: Still Life
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how lighting and arrangement define form and value in a still-life setup.

nodes.title: Landscapes
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify foreground, middle ground, background, and horizon in a landscape.

nodes.title: Portraiture
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the standard placement of facial features on the head.

nodes.title: Digital Drawing Tools
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify core digital-art tools (layers, brushes, opacity, selection) and their uses.

nodes.title: Digital Sketching
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how layers and undo support iterative digital sketching.

nodes.title: Digital Painting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify digital painting techniques (blending modes, custom brushes, color picking).

nodes.title: Photo Manipulation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify masking, compositing, and adjustment tools used to edit photographs.

nodes.title: Texture Painting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how texture brushes and overlays simulate surface detail digitally.

nodes.title: Character Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify silhouette, shape language, and appeal principles in character design.

nodes.title: Environment Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how perspective and atmospheric depth build a believable environment.

nodes.title: Speed Painting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how blocking in large shapes and values first speeds a painting.

nodes.title: Concept Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the purpose of concept art in visualizing designs for production.

nodes.title: Digital Illustration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify stylistic and technical traits of finished digital illustration.

nodes.title: Matte Painting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how matte paintings extend or create photorealistic backgrounds.

nodes.title: 2D Graphic Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how visual hierarchy and alignment organize a 2D graphic layout.

nodes.title: Logo Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify qualities of an effective logo (simple, memorable, scalable, relevant).

nodes.title: Typography
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can classify typefaces (serif, sans-serif, script, display) and identify type anatomy.

nodes.title: Typographic Hierarchy
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how size, weight, and spacing establish reading hierarchy in text.

nodes.title: Kerning & Tracking
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish kerning, tracking, and leading and identify well-spaced type.

nodes.title: Layout Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how grids, margins, and alignment structure a page layout.

nodes.title: Print Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify print-production concepts (bleed, CMYK, resolution, trim) for print work.

nodes.title: Branding
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the components of a brand identity system (logo, palette, type, voice).

nodes.title: Package Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how dieline, structure, and hierarchy function in package design.

nodes.title: UI/UX Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish UI (visual interface) from UX (user flow) concerns in a design.

nodes.title: Web Design
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify responsive-layout and accessibility considerations in web design.

nodes.title: Animation Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how a sequence of frames creates the illusion of motion (persistence of vision).

nodes.title: 2D Animation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify keyframes, in-betweens, and timing in a 2D animation.

nodes.title: 3D Basics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify core 3D concepts (mesh, vertex, camera, lighting) in a 3D scene.

nodes.title: Stop Motion
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how incremental physical movements captured frame-by-frame create stop motion.

nodes.title: Motion Graphics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how animated typography and shapes communicate in motion graphics.

nodes.title: Character Animation
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the twelve principles of animation applied to character movement.

nodes.title: Rigging
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the purpose of a skeleton, joints, and controls in a character rig.

nodes.title: VFX
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify common visual-effects elements (particles, simulation, keying) in a shot.

nodes.title: Compositing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how layers, mattes, and color grading combine elements in a final composite.

nodes.title: AI-Assisted Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI tools in an art workflow.

nodes.title: Style Transfer
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how style transfer applies the visual style of one image to another.

nodes.title: Prompt Crafting
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how subject, style, and modifier terms shape an AI image prompt.

nodes.title: Art Ethics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify ethical issues in art (attribution, plagiarism, training-data consent, fair use).

nodes.title: Creative Coding
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how loops, variables, and coordinates generate visuals in creative coding.

nodes.title: Generative Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can explain how rules, randomness, and parameters drive generative artwork.

nodes.title: Machine Learning
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how a model learns patterns from training data at a conceptual level.

nodes.title: Neural Networks
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the basic structure of a neural network (layers, nodes, weights).

nodes.title: Art History Survey
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can place major art periods in rough chronological order.

nodes.title: Prehistoric & Ancient Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify hallmark works of prehistoric, Egyptian, Greek, and Roman art.

nodes.title: Renaissance Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify Renaissance innovations (linear perspective, realism, key artists).

nodes.title: Impressionism
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify Impressionist traits (visible brushwork, light, everyday subjects) and artists.

nodes.title: Modern Art: Cubism & Surrealism
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can distinguish Cubism from Surrealism by their defining visual characteristics.

nodes.title: Contemporary Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify features of contemporary art movements (conceptual, digital, installation).

nodes.title: Art Criticism: Describe & Analyze
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can describe the subject and analyze the use of elements and principles in an artwork.

nodes.title: Art Interpretation & Judgment
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can interpret an artwork's meaning and justify a judgment using visual evidence.

nodes.title: Aesthetics
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify differing aesthetic theories about what makes an object a work of art.

nodes.title: Portfolio Development
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify what makes a strong, cohesive portfolio for a target audience.

nodes.title: Art Critique
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can give and receive specific, constructive critique using art vocabulary.

nodes.title: Art Business
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify basic art-business concepts (pricing, contracts, licensing, rights).

nodes.title: Teaching Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify effective ways to sequence and explain an art skill to a learner.

nodes.title: Freelancing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the workflow of a freelance art project from inquiry to delivery.

nodes.title: Client Work
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how a creative brief and revision rounds shape client work.

nodes.title: Art Direction
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the art director's role in setting and maintaining visual direction.

nodes.title: Marketing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify channels and tactics artists use to market their work.

nodes.title: Networking
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify effective professional networking practices for artists.

nodes.title: Scientific Illustration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the accuracy and clarity conventions of scientific illustration.

nodes.title: Medical Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how medical illustration communicates anatomy and procedures clearly.

nodes.title: Botanical Art
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the botanical-accuracy conventions used to depict plants.

nodes.title: Technical Drawing
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify orthographic views and dimensioning conventions in a technical drawing.

nodes.title: Architectural Rendering
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify how perspective, light, and material cues create an architectural rendering.

nodes.title: Fashion Illustration
nodes.mastery_criteria: Student can identify the elongated proportions (croquis) used in fashion illustration.

merges.note: Overlap Foundations: C2 'Basic Art Skills' overlaps CR-001 'Foundational Drawing'. CR-001 is the canonical drawing-spine entry; C2 RETAINED as the broader K-3 tools/materials umbrella (spans non-drawing media) and soft-wired to CR-001. Both distinct game skills; no node removed. C2 keeps its cross-domain edges (Tech T28->C2, Social SS24->C2, Math M-087->C2).

Overlap Design: C5 'Visual Design Principles' is the umbrella for the new Principles of Design atomics (CR-304..CR-310) and overlaps CR-014 'Composition' (their applied synthesis). C5 RETAINED as the principles hub (soft dep of the atomics); CR-014 canonical for arranging elements on the picture plane. Both retained. C5 keeps cross-domain edges (C5->Tech T28, Tech T-SD030->C5, English E25->C5).

Overlap Visual Arts: C16 'Visual Arts' is a genre-survey umbrella overlapping the hands-on drawing/painting spine rooted at CR-001. CR-001 canonical; C16 RETAINED as the survey node (distinguishing drawing/painting/print/sculpture). Both retained; no cross-domain edges on C16.

Overlap Digital: C19 'Digital Art & Design' overlaps the digital-art spine at CR-004 'Digital Drawing Tools' (and CR-005 2D Graphic Design). CR-004 canonical tool-skills entry; C19 RETAINED as the raster-vs-vector survey umbrella. Both retained. C19 keeps its cross-domain edge (C19->Tech T28).
